transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We have the Meridian outbound license on the table for next week, and under our standard transaction process, I'll be conducting the final legal checkpoint today. Before I can record the binding license decision, I need to hear from each of you in turn — patent, R&D, and commercial. Let's start with the patent representative's report. Who would like to go first?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something critical before we proceed. While reviewing our 2018 university license and its executed amendment, I confirmed that we are only permitted to grant exclusivity for industrial analytics fields. Healthcare and other fields must remain available to the company. I have not yet circulated this restriction in the current license-markup thread, but it directly affects the scope of exclusivity we can offer Meridian under the current draft.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical issue on the R&D side. I checked the current prototype and confirmed that component U-7 is owned by a university and is not covered by our company's sublicense rights. The outbound license to Meridian must exclude U-7 and require written university consent before any licensed deployment containing it. I have lab-record confirmation of this but it hasn't yet been added to the transaction checklist.

transcript.text: I need to share something critical from the commercial side before we proceed. During a client-priority call this week, Meridian's general counsel told me directly that Meridian will only proceed with this license if it may sublicense the licensed analytics to its named distributor, Orion Industrial. He also confirmed that the company must retain ownership and use of all background technology and newly developed improvements. I recorded this instruction in my relationship notes, but it has not yet been incorporated into the draft term sheet. This is a deal-critical condition from Meridian that our current draft does not reflect.
